stories.headline: AI inference chip startup Nano-core Chip raises over RMB 1 billion in Series C2 funding
stories.script: Our lead story today. Hangzhou-based AI inference chip developer Nano-core Chip has raised more than RMB 1 billion in Series C2 funding, the company announced on October 28. The round was led by JianTou Investment, with participation from Hangzhou Capital, Kaitai Capital, and other investors. The company will use the proceeds for product development and preparation for volume production.
stories.whyThisMatters: Hangzhou-based AI inference chip developer Nano-core Chip has raised more than RMB 1 billion in Series C2 funding, the company announced on October 28.
keyPoints: AI inference chip startup Nano-core Chip raises over RMB 1 billion in Series C2

stories.headline: Former Xiaomi executive launches smart ring and AI-powered sleep system
stories.script: In China. ISHO, the sleep technology startup founded by former Xiaomi executive Wang Teng, unveiled its first products on October 29: the ISHO Ring smart ring and the iFlow bed temperature-control system. Prices start at RMB 1,799 and RMB 9,999, respectively. The ring monitors physiological signals to track sleep and provide daily energy-management insights.

stories.headline: Ghost in the machine: how AI is haunting the search for the supernatural
stories.script: Around the world. Ghost hunting has changed in recent years due to AI chatbots, and paranormal enthusiasts are concerned Ghost hunting is a tech-heavy pursuit. When Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting investigate haunted locations, they’re loaded up with software of their own design, such as an app that assigns signals from a phone’s sensors to different words in a database. In the age of ChatGPT, the ghost-hunting pair is probing the world of AI. They describe one of their latest inventions, an app called GhostTube Seer , as “the world’s first AI Ghost Hunting tool”. In the hands of paranormal investigators, scientific tools like EMF meters (used to detect electromagnetic fields) are repurposed to identify changes and anomalies that they believe indicate supernatural activity.
stories.whyThisMatters: Ghost hunting has changed in recent years due to AI chatbots, and paranormal enthusiasts are concerned Ghost hunting is a tech-heavy pursuit.
keyPoints: Ghost in the machine: how AI is haunting the search for the supernatural

stories.headline: Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk?
stories.script: Elsewhere. Nvidia's 3 billion dollars investment in Meta's share sale, announced Tuesday, is the latest addition to a portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees that has made the chip giant what some analysts describe as the central bank of the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia also has around 36 billion dollars in cloud backstops and a guarantee of up to 105 billion dollars linked to an OpenAI data center, according to US media.
